title: Automated Safe Reversion Engine with Confidence Scoring and Ripple Detection
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal: Implement an Automated Safe Reversion Engine (ASRE) that performs automatic, auditable reverts for configuration changes that negatively affect cost or reliability while minimizing false positives and blast radius. ASRE will combine three signals: post-deploy telemetry regression detection (latency/cost/error), a confidence scoring model, and a ripple-impact detector that identifies related routes/resources likely to be affected by a revert.

Scope:
- Integrate with existing deployment pipeline so config changes (console/API/infra) generate a monitored rollout context.
- Use lightweight anomaly detection (p99 latency, token cost per request, error rate) + business rules to surface regressions within the canary window.
- Produce a probabilistic confidence score (0.0-1.0) that summarizes signal strength and rule concordance.
- Allow configurable threshold policies per team/route (auto-revert threshold, remediation-only threshold).
- Before auto-revert, run ripple detection to locate collateral resources (e.g., shared KV cache, batching config, routing policy) and estimate revert impact.
- Perform a staged reversion flow: simulated dry-run, read-only rollback probe, automated revert with canary-step if safe, and post-revert verification.
- Emit audit trail entries, PR link to the revert, and a suggested follow-up changelist for root-cause.

Acceptance criteria:
1) ASRE triggers an automated revert in a test harness (staging) for a synthetic config that increases token cost by >30% while keeping false positive rate <5% across 50 runs.
2) Confidence scoring API is available for Console and SDKs; teams can set thresholds per-route.
3) Ripple detector flags dependent routes in >90% of seeded dependency graphs in the simulation suite.
4) All reverts produce an immutable audit record (who/what/why) and a generated GitHub PR + rollback changelog entry.
5) Feature gated and disabled by default for existing production customers; opt-in via Console or infra flag.

Notes on approach and trade-offs:
- We will prioritize telemetry signals that are inexpensive to compute in real-time (e.g., aggregated counters and percentiles) to avoid introducing additional cost.
- The confidence model will be lightweight — a logistic regression / ensembling of rule votes — to keep behavior explainable and auditable for SRE/Compliance.
- Ripple detection uses a dependency graph built from routing configs, tag inheritance, and recent deployment metadata; building a perfect graph is expensive, so we trade completeness for precision and provide human-in-the-loop overrides.
- To reduce customer surprise, auto-reverts will not change model versions or region routing without explicit enterprise opt-in.

Open design decisions:
- Threshold defaults (we propose 20% cost spike OR 15% latency increase OR doubling of error rate in the canary window) — needs PM review.
- Whether rollback should support partial reverts (per-route) or only whole-config reverts — preferring per-route where possible to reduce blast radius.
- Integration with Optimize recommendations: ASRE should consume batching/caching hints to propose safer reverts (e.g., revert a batching buffer change instead of a model change).

Relevant artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ASRE+Spec, PRD: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/asre-prd, simulation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/asre-sim, initial spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2164
